title: Reports of Platform Workers Suffering Injuries in Course of Work
what_it_is: Reports of Platform Workers Suffering Injuries in Course of Work

sections.label: Platform worker injury data reporting
sections.summary: Platform workers lack mandatory work injury compensation, so data is not reported; the Government accepted recommendations to strengthen protection and will mandate reporting once the framework is implemented.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Platform workers are currently not covered by mandatory work injury compensation requirements, so platform work injury data is not reported to the Ministry.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: The Government has accepted recommendations by the Advisory Committee on Platform Workers, including strengthening financial protection in case of work injury.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Upon implementation of the work injury compensation framework for platform workers, the reporting of work injuries for platform workers will be mandated.

sections.label: Platform versus WICA coverage gap
sections.summary: Platform companies' death or permanent disability coverage is largely $10,000 to $30,000, compared to employees' WICA entitlement of up to $289,000, so the Committee recommended the same scope and level.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: For example, platform companies' coverage for death or permanent disability is largely in the $10,000 to $30,000 range, compared to employees' entitlement under WICA of up to $289,000.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: That is a significant difference in the magnitude of coverage.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: This is why the Platform Workers Advisory Committee recommended requiring platform companies to provide the same scope and level of work injury compensation as employees' entitlement under WICA.

sections.label: Compensation varying by earnings
sections.summary: The Platform Workers Advisory Committee recommended that compensation for platform workers should vary based on workers' earnings, the same way WICA operates for injured employees.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The Platform Workers Advisory Committee recommended that compensation for platform workers should vary based on workers' earnings, the same way that WICA operates today for injured employees.

sections.label: Medical expenses for platform workers
sections.summary: Employees are covered for up to $45,000 in medical expenses, so platform workers should not have to rely on MediShield Life, MediSave or out-of-pocket cash for work injuries.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Given that employees are covered for up to $45,000 in medical expenses for work injuries by their employers, there is no reason why platform workers should have to rely on MediShield Life which they pay for using their own MediSave, and consequently, pay part of the medical bills using their MediSave or out-of-pocket cash if they suffer a work injury.

sections.label: Interim WICA-level protection proposal
sections.summary: Insurers said cost-effective coverage was not possible, so GIA members were urged to work with platform companies to offer WICA-level protection by the first quarter of next year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Our discussions with insurers showed it was not possible to do so in a cost-effective way.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: But given the confidence that GIA has on the efficiency of existing products and policies that they have and the public statements by various platform companies that platform workers deserved protection for injuries incurred in the course of their work, I would suggest that GIA members work closely with platform companies to offer financial protection and compensation for these workers at the level of WICA as soon as possible by the first quarter of next year, hopefully, using their existing products while maintaining the cost of premiums at parity with WICA insurance products.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: This will provide better coverage for the workers in the interim and keep costs manageable for platform companies and consumers while we work on implementation details of WICA for this group of workers by the end of 2024.

sections.label: Consumer surveys and street hail
sections.summary: Surveys showed 70% to 90% of consumers would pay up to 10% more for workers' protection, and including street hail would cause an uneven playing field.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Our surveys before the release also showed that consumers in various surveys, between 70% and 90% are prepared to pay up to 10% more in prices to make sure that these workers have the adequate protection, so long as the price increase that they pay for goes directly to helping these workers address their income retirement, their retirement adequacy as well as their ability to have housing adequacy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Specific to the comment that the Member raised about Grab's statement expressing that – excluding street hails from these recommendations would create an unlevel playing field.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: I would say that, in fact, including street hail into this recommendation would cause an uneven playing field instead.
